name: pipeline
description: The IR executor: topological parallel scheduling over the desugared DAG, CEL condition evaluation on unrolled conditional chains, run-time generate expansion over user data-source items, failure propagation with skip semantics, and run reporting. The module that runs the reference workflows.

requirements.title: Topological parallel execution
requirements.description: Execute the IR with Kahn-style readiness scheduling: a node becomes eligible when all its edges (data references plus ordering) are satisfied; eligible nodes run concurrently in goroutines; tie-breaking is deterministic (stable name order). The executed graph is the desugared IR — the scheduler never sees loops or sugar. The scheduling points additionally honor the durable cooperative pause marker: once seen, no slot is granted and nothing new dispatches, outstanding workers drain and settle normally, and the run ends with a paused run-end record and its own exit code (4, below failure and halt in precedence).

requirements.title: Conditional steps via CEL
requirements.description: A node's when: condition is a CEL expression over completed step results (steps.X.field) and params. Conditions are compiled at validate time and evaluated at readiness; false means skipped (a distinct terminal state, not failure), and skip propagates through the unrolled loop chains so a settled loop terminates early.

requirements.title: Generate expansion
requirements.description: A generate node invokes its declared data-source command (opaque user command emitting {items: [{id, deps, ...}]}), validates the item shape, and instantiates the named sub-workflow once per item — item fields bound into the instance's params, inter-instance edges derived from each item's deps (edges to items outside the set are ignored). Expansion happens at run time; the expanded subgraph joins the running DAG.

requirements.title: Failure propagation and skip semantics
requirements.description: When a step fails (final, after retries), every transitive dependent is marked skipped with the failed ancestor recorded; independent branches continue to completion. A halted step propagates the same walk with its own marking (skipped-halt naming the halting step) and its own run exit code, distinct from failure. Terminal step states are exactly: ok, failed, halted, skipped (condition false), skipped (dependency failed), skipped (halt); deferral is non-terminal — a deferred step later settles into one of these, its record annotated with the defer history.

requirements.title: Run reporting
requirements.description: After the run settles, aggregate the journal into a run report: per-step status, duration, attempts, key output fields, and per-generate-item rollups, printed human-readably in stable config order and emittable as JSON. The report is derived from the journal, never from in-memory state alone.

requirements.title: Reference workflow execution
requirements.description: The executor runs the reference orchestrator.yaml end-to-end: the task workflow's unrolled review/fix chain settles on the approval condition and its merge step runs only when approved, and the epic workflow's generate node fans out task sub-workflows over the data-source items with dependency-respecting order, each instance settling through its own merge.

requirements.title: Deferred: generate edge cases
requirements.description: Backlog (design edge case 2): generate with an empty item set (no-op vs error, policy flag), malformed data-source output (validation error contract), and dependency cascade policy when one item's sub-workflow fails (skip dependents only vs abort the fan-out). First pass: empty set is a no-op, malformed output fails the generate node, cascade follows standard skip semantics.

requirements.title: Concurrency bounds
requirements.description: Beside the run-wide --max-parallel semaphore the scheduler honours two declared bounds: a generate's max_parallel (at most N of that generate's instances hold a box slot at once, one pool per generate node) and lanes (IR-declared name -> max; every box of a template that names a lane holds one of its slots). All three are granted together in deterministic id order before a launch and released together at settlement or defer; a held node steps aside without blocking the nodes behind it. The first time a ready node is held it emits step-waiting with the reason (slot n of m, generate <id> n of m, lane <name> n of m), once per distinct reason.

requirements.title: Boundary stop
requirements.description: For every loop with an expectation the scheduler runs the expect command host-side at the loop's entry — before its first iteration's first node dispatches, after the node's own condition so an iteration the loop no longer needs costs no call — and again at every iteration boundary. A count over the cap pauses the run (nothing further dispatches, in-flight steps settle and journal, run-end paused, exit 4) with the detail '<loop>: expected N, cap M; raise the cap and resume'; a failing or malformed command fails the triggering node with the source-contract reason; otherwise the count is emitted as loop-expected and dispatch continues. Never a prompt: runs are unattended.

requirements.title: Deferred: concurrency control
requirements.description: Backlog (design edge case 5): a scheduler-level parallelism cap aware of host resources (CPU, local GPU) and API rate classes. Declared bounds exist (Concurrency bounds: per-generate max_parallel and lanes beside --max-parallel); the resource-aware sizing of the dispatch window remains reserved.

requirements.title: Progress event stream
requirements.description: The run's heartbeat is a typed event stream, not a log line: the scheduler emits step-started (per box attempt), step-settled (every terminal state, with reason, cached flag and span), step-deferred, generate-expanded, pause-requested, and run-ended events to an injected sink (nil = none); the pipeline never renders. The heartbeat slog lines drop to debug. Every box attempt additionally streams its combined container output into <attempt>/output.log, always on, scrubbed with its attempt dir.

requirements.title: Human run vocabulary
requirements.description: Human renderings — the report's text form and the progress stream — never use the scheduler's skip encodings. A loop reads as iterations ran of up to its cap (iterations past convergence are unused cap, not listed), a guard-false step inside an executed iteration is not needed, steps past a failure or halt are not reached with the ancestor and the range; status words are lower-case for the routine and upper-case for what needs the eye (FAIL, HALT, WAIT); text is plain ASCII, one cell per character, in dependency order. The report folds loops into rollups (journal plus IR, selector-independent: the cap is the highest iteration present) beside the complete per-node list the JSON keeps. The progress renderer folds node ids into breadcrumbs with iteration and cap, prints at start and settle only, collapses unused cap and not-reached iterations into one line per loop, and colours the status word alone from the 16 palette slots when the terminal allows; a JSON-lines sink serves machines.

requirements.title: Deferred: observability
requirements.description: Backlog (design edge case 8), now mostly delivered: the status view over the journal of an in-flight run is the tui module (Live observability). What remains reserved is tracing — per-step traces beyond output.log and the session transcripts.

components.name: Scheduler
components.description: Readiness-driven parallel execution over the IR: in-degree tracking, deterministic ready queue, goroutine-per-step with a semaphore cap, terminal-state accounting, failure and halt propagation via dependent traversal, defer(until) re-queueing, and the cooperative pause gate (the durable marker probed at scheduling points; drain-and-settle, then a paused run-end). Consults the journal for resume skips and the meter for admission. Owns the host-side run-prep seam that assembles each infra.RunSpec, including staging the resolved skills leg into the single read-only /faber/skills mount — a per-attempt copy of real files for named skills (not a symlink farm, whose targets would dangle across the bind into the container), a direct mount for the inline skills-root — and, when the per-run sessions toggle is on and the template's invocation profile names a session_dir, the per-attempt live sessions bind (<attempt>/sessions mounted read-write at $HOME/<session_dir>, host-pre-owned like the result dir) that captures the harness's native transcripts crash-safely; the same seam gives interactive re-entry its session-resuming entry (a copy of the saved session mounted over $HOME/<session_dir> and the profile's resume_argv as entry, bare shell on --shell or when nothing was saved). Grants, beside the global semaphore, each generate's instance pool and the declared lanes in one id-ordered pass, announcing a hold once per reason. Emits the typed progress stream (started per attempt, settled, deferred, waiting, expanded, paused, run-ended) to the executor's event sink, journals a start record at every box attempt, and points each attempt's RunSpec.Output at the durable output.log.

components.name: ConditionEvaluator
components.description: CEL environment and lifecycle: validate-time compilation of when: expressions, the steps/params activation built from completed results, and skip decisions at readiness time.

components.name: GenerateExpander
components.description: Run-time fan-out: invokes the data-source command, validates the items contract, instantiates the named sub-workflow per item with param binding and deps-derived edges, and splices the expansion into the running DAG. Owns the deferred empty-set/malformed-source/cascade policies.

components.name: RunReporter
components.description: Aggregates the settled run from the journal into the human summary and JSON report: stable ordering, per-step lines, generate-item rollups, failure diagnostics with handoff pointers, halt blocks naming the halting step and reason, and the paused-run flag and footer (a paused run reads as deliberately incomplete, naming the resume command). Folds unrolled loops back into rollups (iterations ran of up to cap, executed iterations nested, not-reached ranges) for the human text, which reads in dependency order with the human vocabulary (ok / FAIL / HALT / not needed / not reached) while the JSON keeps every node; owns the progress renderers over the scheduler's event stream — the breadcrumb text sink with palette-only colour and the JSON-lines sink. Owns the deferred live-observability seam.

data_flows.name: IR execution flow
data_flows.description: Validated IR + params -> scheduler readiness loop -> (condition check -> journal lookup -> meter admission -> box run -> result record) per step -> generate expansion splices item subgraphs -> journal appends -> settled run -> report.
